title: Turn Into a Palindrome
solution: Pairs of mirrored positions (i, n+1-i) are independent. If s_i equals s_{n+1-i} the pair costs 0. If they differ and one of them already equals c, overwrite the other with c for cost 1. If they differ and neither is c, both must become c (the only reachable common letter), costing 2. Sum over the floor(n/2) pairs; the middle character of odd n never matters. O(n) per test.
solution_check: Hand-checked all 5 samples pair by pair: abca/b=1, xyx=0, abcbb/e=2, adbccbad/d=2, codeforces/c=1+2+1+2+2=8.

rejected_patterns.reason: No choice is being made: each mismatched mirrored pair must end up as c (the only letter you can write), so the cost of 1 or 2 is forced. There is no greedy choice or exchange argument, so the label is filler.
Just a loop over i and n-1-i to visit mirrored pairs, which is ordinary palindrome scaffolding. No pointer is moved based on a condition, so it is not the two-pointers technique.

rejected_tags.reason: Same as the pattern: the per-pair cost is forced, and nothing greedy is decided.

notes.solver: Very easy Div-level A; per-pair case analysis. two-pointers only in the sense of scanning mirrored ends, low confidence. No DP needed.
notes.skeptic: Checked with code on all 5 samples: [1,0,2,2,8] matches. The pair costs are 0 if the pair matches, 1 if the pair differs and contains c, and 2 otherwise. This is a trivial Div A.
